newsitem.title: LATVIA: Vote on new Latvian finmin expected this week.
newsitem.headline: Vote on new Latvian finmin expected this week.

text.p: A vote to confirm proposed new Latvian finance minister Robert Zile is expected this week after the largest of the ruling government parties supported him on Tuesday, politicians said.
The finance minister's post has been controversial and a row over it caused the fall of the previous government of Prime Minister Andris Shkele.
The Democratic Party Saimnieks decided at a meeting to back Zile, who is to fill a post vacant since October. Other key parties have already said they support Zile.
"We believe the vote of confidence (on Zile) will take place on Thursday," Andrej Panteleev, head of the parliament faction of second-largest party, Latvia's Way, told journalists.
He said the final procedural details would be discussed at a Wednesday meeting of the committee which groups the eight parties that form the government.
Shkele's previous government fell after President Guntis Ulmanis called on parliament to reject a previous candidate for the post. Shkele was furious and resigned.
Shkele and the president later patched up their differences and Shkele formed a new government, which was confirmed in office on February 13.
Zile, 38, is a member of the third largest party in the eight-party ruling coalition, Fatherland and Freedom, and is currently head of the parliament budget and finance committee.
He is an economist by profession but has been in politics since the late 1980s when the movement began to regain Latvia's independence from the Soviet Union.
He has also been on the board of leading bank Unibanka, Riga commercial port and the Latvian Privatisation Agency. -- Martinsh Gravitis, Riga Newsroom + 371 721 5240
